source.title: On the Effect of Pretraining Corpora on In-context Learning by a Large-scale Language Model
source.authors: Seongjin Shin; Sang-Woo Lee; Hwijeen Ahn; Sungdong Kim; Hyoungseok Kim; Boseop Kim; Kyunghyun Cho; Gichang Lee; W. Park; Jung-Woo Ha; Nako Sung

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation perplexity and downstream in-context task performance across corpus and token-count conditions. This is a different measurement from fitting scaling laws, but it directly tests the downstream-predictability version.
record.gate_note: The paper does not fit power laws for held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; extrapolate loss from small runs; or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its relevant results compare validation perplexity or pretraining token count with downstream in-context performance. The rows retain selected task-specific comparisons emphasized in the text, the reported token-count sweep, and the stated within-model training-step relationship.
record.test_reason: The study gives results and an explicit argument on whether validation perplexity and corpus size predict downstream in-context performance (V6). Across 1.3B models trained on different corpora, low perplexity does not imply good few-shot performance. Within one training run, the two correlate. It fits no loss scaling laws, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that corpus source strongly determines whether in-context learning emerges, and that corpus size does not by itself determine it. Combining corpora can make ICL emerge even when neither corpus does alone. Domain relevance helps zero-shot but does not guarantee few-shot performance. PPL correlates with ICL within one training run but does not predict few-shot differences across models trained on different corpora.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies pretraining corpus sources and sizes and measures perplexity and in-context task performance; it does not fit the original scaling-law models or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The PPL-to-few-shot relationship differs between tracking one model through training and comparing models trained on different corpus sources. Corpus source and corpus size also change downstream performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Corpus source and corpus combination determine whether few-shot in-context learning emerges, independent of size. KiN+Ency and Cafe+KiN produce ICL; Cafe+News at 150B does not. LoRA fine-tuning differences across corpora are small (Table 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream in-context ability depends on pretraining data composition in ways not captured by loss or data size.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2022
record.problems: The study uses HyperCLOVA models and Korean downstream tasks; the token-count sweep uses a single model size and only three token counts. The authors say evaluation on larger models is left for future work. Figure 4's relationship is described in text but its plotted values are not transcribed here.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 and Tables 3-5 report additional corpus-model/task combinations, including zero-shot results; not all individual task metrics are listed here because the text emphasizes selected few-shot comparisons for the PPL-predictability question. Figure 3 also compares 1.3B- and 6.9B-sized models at two corpus sizes; the text gives a qualitative description, but no task-specific values are transcribed here.

untested.parts: No fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
Text only. Data repetition is varied (6B/56B unique data over about 150B training tokens), but no power-law form is fitted.
No exponents are fitted or compared.
Parameter scaling is covered only qualitatively (1.3B vs 6.9B, Figure 3, no numbers). No functional fit of downstream performance against scale or loss. Only three data sizes are used.

missing.what: Blog corpus-size sweep: Blog 150B (PPL 152.40, EM 50.74), Blog 54B (155.69, 49.13), Blog 27B (165.60, 10.91). The authors say size affects performance more than PPL.
Same-size 27B corpus models (Blog/Cafe/News/Comments 27B), with PPL and few-shot scores at controlled size
Combined-corpus PPL vs performance: Cafe+News PPL 154.20 but poor scores (YNAT 8.19); KiN+Ency PPL 164.69 with ICL emerging
Zero-shot performance correlates more with PPL than few-shot does, with Modu as an exception
Scatter of PPL vs normalized few-shot performance across corpus models
1.3B vs 6.9B models at 56B and 150B unique tokens: the 56B decrease is not significant at 6.9B either

record.verdict_notes: The 'tokens' sweep varies unique data at a fixed compute of 72K steps (about 150B tokens seen), not training tokens. The study is NAACL 2022, not one of the original sources. Rows r19–r23 rest on one qualitative sentence about Figure 4.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling-law fit of held-out loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute optimization or parameter/token allocation trend is measured.
No comparison of architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns Korean text pretraining; it does not test other modalities or the listed training regimes.
It tests in-context downstream performance against validation perplexity and training-token count in HyperCLOVA settings, not general downstream performance across models, tasks, or training regimes.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Blog
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on the Blog corpus; evaluated in-context few-shot on KorQuAD.
rows.note: The authors identify Blog as having the lowest PPL and best in-context performance overall.
rows.check: A single model's score shows no relationship by itself. It is kept as the consistent endpoint: Blog has the lowest PPL (152.40) and the best performance. Baseline should be Majority (0.0 EM).

rows.subject: Cafe
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on the Cafe corpus; evaluated in-context few-shot on KorQuAD.
rows.note: The paper notes Cafe has the second-lowest PPL among the domain models but does not show competitive few-shot ability.
rows.check: This row is evidence against PPL predicting performance. Cafe has the second-lowest PPL (170.85) but few-shot ability does not emerge (3.12 EM). State should be absent, not partial.

source_check.correct: Cafe corpus size: 82.5B tokens; training exposure: about 150B tokens over 72K steps. Majority KorQuAD EM baseline: 0.0.
source_check.problem: Corpus size is mislabeled as training exposure; the table supplies a Majority baseline.

rows.check: KiN has the third-lowest PPL (187.80) yet only 4.85 EM; the authors say few-shot ability was not observed. State should be absent, not partial.

rows.subject: Ency

rows.check: Ency has the highest PPL and the worst performance, which is consistent with PPL predictability. Partial is wrong. Note that Ency used a 12K-step early-stopped checkpoint.

rows.subject: News
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on the News corpus; evaluated in-context few-shot on YNAT.

rows.check: This is a domain-relevance result (Section 4.5), not a PPL or scale test. News's high PPL (234.78) and poor YNAT score (14.36) are not a discordance for V6.

rows.subject: Modu
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on the Modu corpus; evaluated in-context few-shot on YNAT.
rows.note: The paper notes Modu performs better than Cafe and News despite having less than one-tenth their corpus size; its PPL is relatively high.
rows.check: Modu has relatively high PPL (226.01) and the smallest corpus (5.9B), yet beats Cafe and News on YNAT (43.27). This contradicts both PPL and corpus size as predictors, so 'observed' is the wrong direction.

source_check.correct: Modu corpus size: 5.9B tokens; training exposure: about 150B tokens over 72K steps. Majority YNAT F1 baseline: 8.26. State: reversed for the cross-corpus prediction comparison; Modu has higher PPL but higher YNAT F1 than Cafe and KiN.
source_check.problem: Corpus size is mislabeled, a stated baseline is omitted, and the comparative ranking reverses the predicted direction.

relationships.condition: Comparing 1.3B few-shot models trained on different single corpora at a matched training budget
relationships.reason: Low-PPL Cafe and KiN models fail at few-shot (r2, r3, r6, r7). High-PPL, small-corpus Modu outperforms them (r8). The authors say PPL is not a strong predictor across corpora.
relationships.display_finding: Low-perplexity Cafe and KiN models failed at few-shot learning, while the higher-perplexity Modu model trained on a smaller corpus outperformed them at a matched budget.
